title: Effect of Enzymatic Crosslinking on Gel Strength and Water Holding Capacity of Bovine Gelatin
abstract: Gelatin is a widely used protein ingredient valued for its gelling and water holding properties, but native gelatin gels are often thermally unstable. This study investigated microbial transglutaminase treatment (0 to 10 U/g protein) on bovine hide gelatin. Crosslinked gelatin exhibited a 42% increase in gel strength and improved water holding capacity from 68% to 89% compared to untreated controls. SDS-PAGE confirmed high molecular weight polymer formation. These results suggest enzymatic modification is an effective strategy for enhancing the functional performance of gelatin-based food systems.

title: Ultrasound-Assisted Modification of Egg White Protein Foaming Properties
abstract: Foaming capacity is a critical functional property for protein ingredients used in bakery and confectionery applications. This work examined the impact of high intensity ultrasound (20 kHz, 100 to 400 W) on egg white protein isolate. Ultrasonicated samples showed foaming capacity increased from 112% to 187%, while foam stability after 30 minutes improved by 35%. Particle size analysis revealed partial protein unfolding without significant aggregation. Circular dichroism confirmed secondary structure changes consistent with increased surface hydrophobicity. Ultrasound treatment is proposed as a mild, non-thermal method to enhance egg protein functionality.

title: pH-Shifting Processing Improves Solubility of Whey Protein Isolate Under Acidic Conditions

Treated samples showed solubility increases from 22% to 71% at pH 4.5. Differential scanning calorimetry indicated partial denaturation and refolding during processing. Zeta potential measurements confirmed altered surface charge distribution. The pH-shifting approach offers a practical route to expand whey protein isolate applications in low pH food formulations.

This study used microbial transglutaminase (0 to 10 U/g protein) to crosslink extracted fungal protein and assessed resulting gel strength and water holding capacity. Crosslinked gels showed a 41% increase in storage modulus and improved water holding capacity from 65% to 87%. SDS-PAGE analysis confirmed formation of high molecular weight polymers indicative of enzymatic crosslinking. These findings suggest transglutaminase treatment effectively enhances the gelation functionality of Aspergillus oryzae-derived fungal protein.

title: Optimization of Xanthan Gum Production by Xanthomonas campestris and Characterization of Its Rheological Functional Properties
abstract: Xanthan gum, an exopolysaccharide produced by Xanthomonas campestris through aerobic fermentation, is widely applied as a food thickening and stabilizing agent. This study optimized fermentation carbon source and agitation rate to maximize xanthan yield and evaluated resulting rheological properties. Optimized fermentation conditions achieved a yield of 32 g/L, and the resulting xanthan solutions exhibited apparent viscosity of 850 mPa.s at 10 s-1 shear rate with pronounced shear thinning behavior. Water holding capacity of the hydrated gum reached 24.1 g/g, confirming strong functional hydrocolloid performance. These results support optimized fermentation as an approach for enhancing the functional properties of xanthan gum for food applications.

title: High Pressure Processing Effects on Solubility and Emulsifying Activity of Bacterial Protein Isolate from Cupriavidus necator
abstract: Cupriavidus necator, a hydrogen-oxidizing bacterium, produces protein-rich biomass considered a candidate alternative protein source for food applications. This study subjected extracted bacterial protein isolate to high pressure processing (200 to 500 MPa, 10 min) and measured resulting solubility and emulsifying activity. Solubility increased from 29% to 63% at pH 7 following 400 MPa treatment, while emulsifying activity index rose to 21.7 m2/g. Surface hydrophobicity increased progressively with pressure level, as confirmed by fluorescence probe analysis, up to 400 MPa before declining. These findings indicate moderate high pressure treatment can improve the functional properties of Cupriavidus necator-derived bacterial protein isolate.

title: Deamidation Treatment Improves Solubility and Interfacial Properties of Torula Yeast Protein Concentrate

Deamidated protein exhibited a 3.1 fold increase in solubility at pH 7 and a 37% reduction in oil water interfacial tension. Circular dichroism spectra indicated increased random coil content consistent with reduced protein-protein interactions following treatment. title: Freeze-Drying Parameters Affect Aggregation and Water Holding Capacity of Gellan Gum Produced by Sphingomonas elodea
abstract: Gellan gum, an exopolysaccharide produced by Sphingomonas elodea through aerobic fermentation, is a widely used gelling agent in food systems. This study examined how freeze-drying shelf temperature (minus 40 to minus 15 degrees C) influenced gellan gum aggregation behavior and functional properties upon rehydration. Samples dried at minus 15 degrees C exhibited greater particle aggregation and reduced water holding capacity (9.8 g/g) compared to 16.3 g/g for samples dried at minus 40 degrees C. Scanning electron microscopy revealed denser, more collapsed microstructures at higher drying temperatures. Optimized freeze-drying conditions are recommended to preserve the functional water holding capacity of gellan gum for food applications.

title: Effect of Alkaline Extraction pH on Solubility and Gelation of Protein Isolate from Common Carp Muscle
abstract: Common carp is a widely farmed freshwater fish species with underutilized muscle protein for value added applications. This study extracted protein isolate from carp muscle using alkaline solubilization at pH 10 to 12 and evaluated resulting solubility and gel forming properties. Extraction at pH 11 produced isolate with the highest solubility (74%) and gel storage modulus, compared to lower yields at pH 10. Protein recovery and water holding capacity of formed gels both increased with rising extraction pH up to 11 before declining at pH 12. These findings indicate alkaline extraction pH is a critical parameter for optimizing carp muscle protein isolate functional gelation properties.

title: Effect of Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction on Foaming and Emulsifying Properties of Nannochloropsis Microalgae Protein Concentrate
abstract: Nannochloropsis biomass, cultivated for its high protein and lipid content, has been proposed as a functional food ingredient, though native protein concentrates often show limited surface activity. This study applied high intensity ultrasound (20 kHz, 150 to 400 W) during alkaline extraction of Nannochloropsis protein and evaluated resulting foaming and emulsifying behavior. Ultrasound-assisted extraction increased foaming capacity from 17% to 45% and emulsifying activity index from 12.8 to 26.1 m2/g. Particle size analysis confirmed enhanced cell wall disruption under ultrasound treatment. These results suggest ultrasound-assisted extraction is an effective method for improving the functional properties of Nannochloropsis protein concentrate.

title: pH-Shifting Treatment Improves Gelation Behavior of Chlorella vulgaris Protein Isolate
abstract: Chlorella vulgaris microalgae biomass is a recognized alternative protein source, though its gelation properties remain poorly characterized relative to conventional food proteins. This study applied alkaline pH-shifting (pH 11 for 30 min, followed by isoelectric precipitation) to Chlorella vulgaris protein isolate and evaluated gel formation under heat treatment. Treated protein formed gels with 34% higher storage modulus and improved water holding capacity compared to conventionally extracted isolate. Circular dichroism confirmed increased beta-sheet content associated with the pH-shifting process. The results support pH-shifting as an effective modification method for improving Chlorella vulgaris protein gelation functionality.

title: Enzymatic Hydrolysis Enhances Water Holding Capacity and Viscosity of Laminaria japonica (Kelp) Protein Hydrolysate
abstract: Kelp biomass contains substantial protein that could be valorized for functional food ingredient development, though its native hydration properties are limited. This study used Alcalase hydrolysis (0.5 to 2% enzyme to substrate ratio) to modify Laminaria japonica protein and evaluated resulting water holding capacity and apparent viscosity. Mild hydrolysis (1%) increased water holding capacity from 3.3 to 6.1 g/g while reducing viscosity by 38% at 50 s-1 shear rate. Degree of hydrolysis was confirmed by ninhydrin assay and SDS-PAGE peptide profiling. These results suggest controlled enzymatic hydrolysis is an effective method for improving kelp protein hydrolysate functionality for food applications.

title: High Hydrostatic Pressure Treatment Alters Solubility and Emulsifying Activity of Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) Protein Isolate
abstract: Spirulina protein isolate is a widely studied microalgal ingredient with functional potential in food formulation, though processing effects on emulsifying performance remain incompletely understood. This study subjected Arthrospira platensis protein isolate to high hydrostatic pressure (200 to 500 MPa, 10 min) and measured resulting solubility and emulsifying activity. Solubility increased from 44% to 78% at pH 7 following 400 MPa treatment, while emulsifying activity index rose to 29.3 m2/g. Surface hydrophobicity increased progressively with pressure level up to 400 MPa before declining at higher pressures. These findings indicate moderate high pressure treatment can improve the functional properties of Spirulina protein isolate.

title: Glycation via Maillard Reaction Improves Thermal Stability of Porphyra (Nori) Protein Emulsions
abstract: Porphyra protein extracted from nori seaweed has demonstrated emulsifying potential, but its stability under thermal processing conditions is limited. This study conjugated Porphyra protein with maltodextrin through controlled dry heating (60 degrees C, 65% relative humidity, up to 5 days) to induce glycation. Glycated protein exhibited a 41% improvement in emulsion stability after heating at 90 degrees C and reduced droplet coalescence during 14 days of storage. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed covalent conjugation between protein and polysaccharide chains. Glycation is presented as an effective approach for improving the thermal functional stability of Porphyra protein-based emulsifiers.

title: Transglutaminase Crosslinking Enhances Gel Strength of Undaria pinnatifida (Wakame) Protein Isolate

Crosslinked gels exhibited a 39% increase in gel strength and improved water holding capacity from 60% to 82%. SDS-PAGE analysis confirmed formation of high molecular weight polymers consistent with enzymatic crosslinking. These findings indicate transglutaminase treatment is an effective strategy for improving the gelation functionality of wakame protein isolate.

title: Spray Drying Conditions Influence Rheological Properties and Solubility of Dunaliella salina Protein Concentrate
abstract: Dunaliella salina microalgae biomass has drawn interest as a functional protein source, though drying conditions affecting its solubility remain underexplored. This study evaluated spray drying inlet temperature (150 to 190 degrees C) on the rheological and solubility properties of extracted Dunaliella salina protein concentrate. Protein dried at 170 degrees C retained the highest solubility and lowest viscosity loss, while higher temperatures caused a 32% decline in solubility due to increased denaturation. Differential scanning calorimetry confirmed progressive structural changes with rising drying temperature. Moderate spray drying temperatures are recommended to preserve the functional properties of Dunaliella salina protein concentrate.

title: Deamidation Treatment Enhances Solubility and Interfacial Properties of Gracilaria Red Seaweed Protein Extract
abstract: Gracilaria red seaweed protein extract exhibits limited solubility and interfacial activity at neutral pH, restricting its use in acidic and low ionic strength food systems. This study applied enzymatic deamidation using protein glutaminase to modify Gracilaria protein extract and evaluated resulting functional properties. Deamidated extract showed a 2.7 fold increase in solubility at pH 7 and a 35% reduction in interfacial tension at the oil water interface. Circular dichroism spectra indicated reduced ordered secondary structure content following treatment. The results indicate deamidation is an effective strategy for broadening the functional application range of Gracilaria red seaweed protein extract.

title: Freeze-Drying Process Parameters Affect Aggregation Behavior and Foaming Capacity of Haematococcus pluvialis Protein Isolate
abstract: Haematococcus pluvialis microalgae, primarily cultivated for astaxanthin production, also yields protein-rich biomass with potential functional applications, yet drying-induced structural changes remain underexplored. This study examined how freeze-drying shelf temperature (minus 40 to minus 10 degrees C) influenced Haematococcus pluvialis protein isolate aggregation and foaming capacity. Samples dried at minus 10 degrees C exhibited greater particle aggregation and a foaming capacity decrease to 21%, compared to 48% for samples dried at minus 40 degrees C. Scanning electron microscopy revealed denser, more collapsed microstructures at higher drying temperatures. Optimized freeze-drying conditions are recommended to preserve the functional foaming capacity of Haematococcus pluvialis protein isolate.

title: Microwave-Assisted Extraction Improves Yield and Solubility of Sargassum fusiforme (Hijiki) Protein Concentrate
abstract: Sargassum fusiforme, a brown seaweed traditionally consumed in East Asian cuisine, contains protein that could be valorized for functional food ingredient development, though extraction method strongly influences recovery. This study compared conventional alkaline extraction to microwave-assisted alkaline extraction (700 W, 60 to 180 s) for Sargassum fusiforme protein concentrate and measured resulting yield and solubility. Microwave-assisted extraction increased protein yield from 46% to 69% and improved solubility at pH 7 from 27% to 55%. Particle size analysis indicated more efficient cell wall disruption under microwave treatment. These results suggest microwave-assisted extraction is a practical method for improving both yield and functional solubility of hijiki protein concentrate.

title: Acid Hydrolysis Modification of Chondrus crispus (Irish Moss) Protein for Improved Foaming and Emulsifying Properties

Foaming capacity increased from 9% in native protein to 42% after moderate hydrolysis, while emulsifying activity index rose to 17.4 m2/g. These results suggest acid hydrolysis can substantially improve the functional performance of Irish moss protein extract for food applications.

title: Effect of Alkaline Extraction pH on Viscosity and Water Holding Capacity of Ecklonia cava (Brown Seaweed) Protein Isolate
abstract: Ecklonia cava is a brown seaweed species increasingly explored as a source of functional protein for food applications, though extraction conditions strongly affect its rheological performance. This study evaluated alkaline extraction at pH 9 to 12 on Ecklonia cava protein isolate and assessed resulting apparent viscosity and water holding capacity. Extraction at pH 11 produced protein isolate with the highest water holding capacity (5.9 g/g) and lowest apparent viscosity at 50 s-1 shear rate, compared to lower functionality at pH 9. Protein solubility and extraction yield both increased with rising extraction pH up to 11 before declining at pH 12. These findings indicate that alkaline extraction pH is a critical parameter for optimizing Ecklonia cava protein isolate functional properties.

title: Ultrasonication Alters Structural and Emulsifying Properties of Isochrysis galbana Microalgae Protein Extract
abstract: Isochrysis galbana, a marine microalga cultivated primarily for aquaculture feed, contains protein with potential functional relevance for human food applications that has been little explored. This study applied high intensity ultrasound (20 kHz, 100 to 350 W) to Isochrysis galbana protein extract and evaluated resulting structural and emulsifying changes. Ultrasonicated samples showed emulsifying activity index increases from 10.9 to 22.6 m2/g and emulsion stability improvements of 27% after 24 hours. Surface hydrophobicity increased with treatment intensity, as confirmed by fluorescence probe analysis, without significant protein aggregation. Ultrasound treatment is proposed as a mild processing method to enhance the functional properties of Isochrysis galbana protein extract for food use.
